findings.text: Header helpers expose OF-node extraction from an IRQ domain, CPU-number extraction from a redistributor type value, and setters marking an IRQ as single-target, affinity-on-activate, and resend-when-in-progress.

Preallocated firmware tables are accepted only when the boot redistributor already has LPIs enabled and its property base address falls inside a reserved range sized for the property table; on success the common state records preallocated tables and marks the property base as needing cache flushing.

Boot-time LPI table setup first ensures the shared property table exists, then allocates one pending table page per possible CPU and stores it in that CPU redistributor record, failing the whole step if any allocation fails.

Virtual pending-table handover polls the dirty indicator with bounded relaxed waits, then clears the valid indicator plus caller-selected clear bits while setting caller-selected set bits and re-polls; the returned status flags pending-last when the table still reports dirty after the second wait.

Per-CPU LPI bringup is idempotent per redistributor and has two paths: reuse firmware tables after cross-checking a common property base and reserved pending base, or program property and pending bases with shareable cacheable attributes plus an ID size derived from the LPI bit count with fallback to non-shareable non-cacheable when hardware reports no shareability; it then enables LPIs, preinitializes virtual property ID bits and clears virtual pending valid when virtual LPIs exist without reserved VPE identity, disables virtual features if VPE level-one allocation fails, and orders writes before marking the CPU enabled.

Each online CPU binds one collection per ITS, skipping ITS nodes on a mismatched NUMA node for the affected erratum, selecting either the redistributor physical base or a shifted CPU number from the redistributor type register depending on the ITS physical-target mode, storing target and CPU identity in the collection, then issuing map and invalidate-all for that collection.
Collection bringup for all ITS nodes walks the global ITS list while holding the global ITS lock.
The per-ITS device list is searched and mutated only while holding that ITS lock with interrupts saved, covering lookup by device identity, insertion on creation, and removal on free.

Table backing is located by scanning base registers for a matching type; flat tables enforce an entry-count bound while indirect tables compute a level-one index from entry and chunk sizes, allocate a zeroed second-level page on demand, flush page and entry when the table reports no shareability, install the entry as valid, and order updates before use; device tables without a register fall back to a hardware device-identity limit.

VPE table backing is ensured on every virtualization-capable ITS for the given VPE identity, and on newer hardware with reserved VPE identifiers also in every possible CPU redistributor copy, failing if any piece cannot be backed.

Device setup rounds the vector count up to a power of two clamped by the ITS identifier limit, sizes the translation table from entry size with a minimum, allocates translation storage plus optional global LPI and per-event CPU maps, flushes the table, initializes device fields and its event lock, links it into the ITS list, and maps it; interrupt allocation carves a contiguous power-of-two region from the device bitmap and teardown frees the global LPIs, unmaps, and releases storage.

Repeated MSI preparation for the same device identity reuses the existing device and marks it shared instead of allocating again, while teardown retains shared devices entirely and refuses to free when any LPI bits are still set; a device identity colliding with the VPE proxy device without direct LPIs is rejected.
MSI handling is exposed through prepare and teardown callbacks and IRQ handling through select plus alloc, free, activate, and deactivate callbacks wired in the respective operation tables.
Parent GIC allocation distinguishes firmware-description parents expecting a three-field LPI edge spec from irqchip parents expecting a two-field edge spec and rejects other parents.

IRQ allocation reserves a hardware range, prepares IOMMU MSI state, then per virtual interrupt allocates the parent, records hardware number and chip data, and marks the interrupt single-target with affinity decided on activation and resend when in progress; activation chooses an online CPU, accounts the LPI, records the target CPU, publishes effective affinity, and maps the event, deactivation unaccounts and discards, and free releases the bitmap region, clears per-IRQ data, and frees parents.

Doorbell proxying applies only without reserved VPE identifiers: unmap discards and frees the slot while opportunistically reusing the victim pointer, map evicts the current victim occupant if any then assigns the next slot round-robin with target CPU and maps it, and move either clears the doorbell at the old redistributor with a sync when direct LPIs exist or maps and moves the proxy event to the new collection while updating the CPU map.

Proxy map, unmap, and move paths serialize on the proxy lock with interrupts saved when indirect LPIs are used, while the newer per-CPU invalidate-all writes the invalidate register with virtual and VPE-identity fields while holding that CPU redistributor lock and then waits for sync.
The redistributor type register carries a sixteen-bit CPU number field used to derive collection targets on non-physical-target ITS nodes.

Mismatched preallocated property bases taint the kernel, non-reserved preallocated pending bases warn, failure to allocate the VPE level-one table disables reserved-VPE and virtual-LPI features, and a virtual pending table that never clears dirty logs a rate-limited error.

Observed device record holds owning ITS, translation storage plus size and entry count, an event map with LPI bitmap, per-event CPU map, base and count plus its own lock, numeric device identity, list linkage, and a shared flag.

Observed ITS node holds workaround flags, NUMA node, register base, type capabilities, table descriptors, a list of devices with device-allocation and list locks, per-CPU collections each with target address and collection identity, and a callback providing the MSI base.

Observed redistributor state holds local and global flag words, per-CPU pending page, shared property-table address, physical and virtual register bases, per-CPU lock, and capability indicators for virtual LPIs, reserved VPE identity, and direct LPIs.
